# Innovate UK Contract for Innovation — Boosting Fathers' Engagement to Improve Child Outcomes


## Project Scope

Target group:

- fathers of early-years children (aged 3 to 5) with speech & language needs.

Stated goal:

- To provide co-authored story generation through fathers in the home learning environment, contributing to the school readiness of their children across two EYFS areas; Language & Communication and Personal, Social & Emotional Development.

## Project title: 

“Tomale v2.0 - Scaffolded story creation to drive school readiness through improved paternal engagement in children aged 3 to 5 with additional speech & language needs."

## Key Information:

- Funding type: procurement of R&D services, 100% funded, contract (not grant). No advance payments — monthly in arrears against milestones.
- Size: £200k–£500k inclusive of VAT. ≥50% of value must be directly/exclusively R&D. Costs at fair market value, no profit allowed (for Tomale).
- Dates: projects must start 1 Aug 2026 and end 31 Jul 2027 (12 months)
- Application closes 10 Jun 2026, 11:00.

- Subcontractors allowed for specialist skills only.
- Scored questions: Q6–Q12 (each 1–10, three assessors). Q1–5 + Project Details + Project Impact are not scored.

# General Information

## What are we creating?

A father-focused, home-based digital intervention built on Tomale, our existing bespoke AI-generated story platform. The current software will be extended to tackle the specific barriers that stop fathers of early-years (EYFS) children with speech, language and communication needs from engaging in their child's learning. It gives fathers a low-barrier, creative, shared activity (co-authoring personalised stories with their child) that builds the child's communication and language skills, a core element of school readiness.

The barriers we target:

- Limited familiarity with the everyday techniques that develop children's language such as modelling, asking open-ended questions, and dialogic reading.
- Low confidence, sometimes rooted in a father's past or present literacy challenges, that makes reading aloud feel like a test.
- Limited time and energy due to work obligations.
- A sense of gender roles, that early learning is the mother's domain, often reinforced by a support system that mostly targets mothers.
- Psychological discomfort fathers face when navigating emotionally complex or vulnerable topics (e.g., anxiety, diversity and inclusion, and bullying).

## How it works

We expand on Tomale's current story-generation method in two ways;

1. Guiding the father (driving the learning outcomes)

The existing chatbot will be trained on evidence-based therapeutic techniques that prompt and support the father, in the moment, to use the interactions that develop his child's communication and language such as modelling, open-ended questions and dialogic reading. This lets a father contribute directly to their child's development within the EYFS Communication & Language early learning goals (vocabulary, listening and attention, back-and-forth conversation, narrative-building) without needing prior training or confidence, with the tool scaffolding the technique for him.

2. Removing barriers to participation (driving engagement)

Fathers can choose story templates and archetypes built around the topics they find hardest to broach with their child (verified during father onboarding early in the project) such as everyday worries and big feelings, starting nursery, a new sibling, falling out with friends. We are leveraging the power of storytelling, one of humanity's oldest tools for modelling behaviour and passing on understanding, to let a father approach these indirectly and at lower emotional cost. That eases the burden that stops many dads engaging at all, and gets them interacting more often and more richly.

## Existing Software

Tomale today is a consumer product: its chatbot takes text prompts and generates a personalised, illustrated story for a child to enjoy, with themes and artwork styles to let families choose the look and subject of that story. The project turns both features into something materially different. The chatbot stops just being a story _generator_ and becomes a guided _coaching_ layer. Instead of producing a story for the family, it scaffolds the father's own interaction in real time, prompting the dialogic techniques that develop language, and adapting the story output to the users' responses. The same shared activity now produces a measurable developmental effect, not just a finished book.

The existing 'themes' feature undergoes the same step-change. Where they are currently topical choices, the project replaces them with a library of narrative archetypes targeting specific topics fathers struggle to discuss.

Together, the two changes convert Tomale from a consumer illustrated story-maker into a therapeutically-grounded home-learning intervention, which is a genuine step-change in capability.

## Why it fits this competition

- Hits the named funder priorities:
    - Builds fathers' confidence and identity as a caregiver-educator.
    - Increases the quantity and quality of father-child interaction.
    - Targets the early-years transition point the funder cares about.
    - Reaches fathers who are less visible to mother-oriented services, and adds the under-used "father half" of the home learning environment — where fathers make a unique, non-redundant contribution to children's language.
- The home-learning-environment and early-years focus feeds the funder's 2028 goal of 75% of children reaching a Good Level of Development (EYFS profile). Communication and language and PSED are two of the three EYFS prime areas required for a Good Level of Development, so the outcomes map directly onto the goal.
- Produces a tangible platform output and a real, piloted delivery model.

## DRAFT APPLICATION

## PROJECT DETAILS (not scored)

### Project and scope summary (≤800 words)

Evidence consistently shows fathers make a distinctive, additive contribution to children's language, literacy and cognitive development, and that the quantity and quality of father-child shared reading predicts children's language and literacy outcomes.

However, fathers read with their children less often than mothers and are less likely to be the main reader. This gap is widest precisely where it matters most: in families raising a child with additional needs, where the caregiving burden falls disproportionately on mothers, and fathers of children with additional needs take less part in caring than fathers of children without additional needs.

Demographics studies into these families show greater prevalence of divorce, fathers with 'sole-breadwinner' roles, and fathers facing their own literacy and language issues; all of which serves to raise barriers between often willing fathers and their children's needs.

Tomale v2.0 adapts Tomale; an existing bespoke children's-story platform (TRL 7 - trialled for 3 months in 2025 with 100 active users), into a father-targeted, therapeutically-scaffolded at home intervention. Rather than asking a disengaged father to perform read-aloud, the intervention positions him as co-author. Together with the child they create a personalised, illustrated story, guided by an AI chatbot trained using therapeutic principles of speech & language therapists to promote high-quality, developmentally engaging discussions between father and child, and creating stories using scaffolded narrative structures that focus on topics that fathers find most difficult; such as everyday worries and big feelings, starting nursery, a new sibling, falling out with friends.

Designed in conjunction with speech & language therapists, the activity is an educational, user-friendly, creative endeavour between the father and child, focusing on challenging areas with open-ended follow up questions and conversation that serves to deepen the fathers understanding of the child.

The 12-month Phase 1 will:

- Identify families already in the private SLT pipeline who are willing to participate in the project, including a control group that will continue without the intervention.
- Co-design the story templates and father training programme with RCSLT-registered SLTs
- Develop an assessment criteria that measures paternal involvement throughout the course of the project.
- Develop an assessment method for both paternal involvement and educational outcomes in line with EYFS school readiness goals for language & communication and personal, social & emotional development.
- Develop three novel technical components;
	- A consistent multi-story/multi-style character-illustration pipeline
	- In line with SLT therapeutic approach, several co-authoring chatbot & agent workflows child-safety guardrails, designed to facilitate a detailed dialogue between father and child during story creation.
	- Story archetypes based on topics fathers find most difficult that enable diverse, personalised story creation.
- Run a clinically-supervised pilot with 30 fathers and their early-years children
- Measure paternal engagement in the home learning environment via. in-app behavioural analytics.
- Measure child communication/language outcomes via. SLT and EYFS teacher-administered  assessments, goal attainment and school readiness ratings.
- Produce robust feasibility evidence and a clear post-project exploitation plan.

The final outputs of the project will be;

- A report publishing the findings of the research, highlighting the efficacy of the intervention against the stated goals.
- Tomale v2.0, a fully-functional (TLR 7) software platform containing the novel technical components above
- An exploitation plan targeting private SLTs and EYFS settings (private nurseries & primary schools)

### Public description (≤400 words)

Fathers make a distinctive, additive contribution to children's language, literacy and cognitive development when compared to mothers, and both the quantity and quality of father-child shared reading predict children's language and literacy outcomes. However, fathers read with their children less often than mothers, and are less likely to be the main reader.

This gap can be widest where it matters most. Among families of children with speech, language and communication needs, caregiving often falls disproportionately on mothers, and fathers can face added pressures such being the sole earner status, or managing their own literacy and language difficulties. These issues sadly raise barriers between willing fathers and their children's development.

Tomale v2.0 adapts Tomale, an existing personalised children's-story platform, into a father-targeted, therapeutically-scaffolded home intervention. Rather than asking a disengaged father to perform a read-aloud, it positions him as co-author. Father and child create a personalised, illustrated story together, guided by an AI chatbot designed around speech-and-language-therapy principles to prompt high-quality, developmentally rich conversation. Story archetypes focus on the topics fathers find hardest to broach such as everyday worries and big feelings, starting nursery, a new sibling or falling out with friends.

This targets two core EYFS areas; "Language & Communication" and "Personal, Social & Emotional Development" to improve school readiness in children using Tomale v2.0.

Involving RCSLT-registered speech & language therapists, EYFS teachers and overseen by a 3rd party scientific consultant, the 12-month Phase 1 will:

- Recruit 30 fathers and their early-years children through Royal College of Speech & Language Therapist (RCSLT) members and early-years referral networks, including a control group continuing without the intervention.
- Co-design the story templates and father-training programme with Speech & Language Therapists (SLTs).
- Develop measures of paternal involvement and of child outcomes aligned to EYFS school-readiness goals for communication & language and personal, social & emotional development.
- Develop the enhanced platform: consistent personalised illustrations, SLT-informed co-authoring chatbot workflows with child-safety guardrails, and a library of specifically-designed story archetypes.
- Run a clinically-supervised pilot, measuring father engagement via in-app analytics and child outcomes via SLT and EYFS-teacher assessments.

Main outputs: 

- A published report on the intervention's efficacy against the stated goals
- Tomale v2.0, a fully functional (TRL 7) platform incorporating the new components
- An exploitation plan targeting private SLTs and EYFS settings (private nurseries and primary schools).

## Proposed idea and technology (≤600 words) — "How well does the proposal meet the challenge?"
    

** Appendix allowed: 2×A4 PDF with diagrams (use for theory-of-change diagram + solution architecture). **

**The problem

Fathers make a distinctive contribution to children's language, communication and cognitive development in comparison to mothers.1 Both the quantity and quality of father-child shared reading predicts children's language and early literacy outcomes.2 Yet fathers read with their children less often than mothers and are less likely to be the main reader.3 Among families of children with speech, language and communication needs, the father is often the less involved parent and the one least reached by a support system that tends to engage mothers.4 These children miss the specific benefit an engaged father provides, at exactly the age when communication and language and personal, social and emotional development lay the foundations for school readiness.5

**The solution

Tomale v2.0 repositions the father from reader to co-author. Using an adapted version of the Tomale platform, a father and child create personalised, illustrated stories together by interacting with an AI chatbot. The chatbot follows SLT-designed narrative structures, chosen by the father to suit the desired topic, covering both everyday language-building stories and the topics fathers find hardest to broach, such as big feelings and worries, starting nursery, a new sibling or falling out with friends. Every story is purposeful, confidence-building and targeted at a defined developmental goal.

**How it addresses the competition scope

The AI scaffolding removes practical and confidence barriers by generating the story content and coaching the father's interaction in real time, so he does not need prior training, creative confidence or dedicated preparation time (scope 1). Through repeated co-authoring sessions, the father builds an identity as an active participant in his child's learning and develops the skills to ask open questions, expand on his child's responses and model richer language (scope 2). The coaching chatbot prompts dialogic techniques during the session, directly increasing both the frequency and quality of father-child verbal interaction (scope 3). The SLT-designed story archetypes specifically address transition points such as starting nursery, family changes and managing emotions, giving fathers a structured way to engage with topics they would otherwise avoid (scope 4). Monthly SLT check-ins use the platform's engagement data to guide the father, creating a feedback loop between professional services and the home learning environment, with the father treated as an equal partner in the child's development (scope 5). The platform is available on any device, at any time, reaching fathers regardless of working pattern, living arrangement or relationship with the child's mother, including fathers who are less visible to traditional services (scope 6).

**Why it works

The theory of change is shown in the appendix. The coaching layer (PD-03) is the core mechanism: it scaffolds the father's interaction technique in the moment, so the co-authoring session produces measurable gains in the child's communication and language while supporting their personal, social and emotional development. Both are prime areas of the Early Years Foundation Stage that underpin a Good Level of Development.

**Current state of readiness

Tomale is a working personalised-story platform with a live user base, proven in real-world use at TRL 7. One father used Tomale with his daughter, who has Down syndrome, to create a story welcoming her newborn niece into the world: "It helped my daughter understand her special role as an aunt in a way that felt personal and accessible to her. I'm truly grateful we could share such a beautiful and emotional moment together" (P. Crosland, personal communication, 2026). The components this project develops are new and do not exist in the current product. The consistent multi-story illustration pipeline, the SLT-designed story archetypes and the co-authoring chatbot workflows sit at TRL 2 today. The project will mature them to TRL 7, demonstrated in an operational environment through the supervised pilot. This is genuine R&D, not a mere adaptation of an existing product.

## Q7. Technical project summary (≤600 words) — "How valid is the technical approach?"

The project tackles three technical challenges, building on Tomale's existing production platform. That platform already runs an asynchronous image and text generation pipeline with queued jobs, structured outputs and automated content moderation. This working, real-world-proven foundation de-risks delivery and gives each new component a measurable baseline to improve on.

**Character-consistent illustration (PD-01):**

Maintaining a child's chosen character reliably across many pages, several stories and different art styles is an unsolved problem in current generative image models, and it is the main quality limit of the present DALL-E-based image generation pipeline, where identity relies on prompt engineering and sometimes drifts across pages. 

PD-01 benchmarks Stability models on Amazon Bedrock against the current Tomale baseline (Dall-E), then fine-tuning SDXL with per-style LoRA adapters and an image-prompt adapter, processed in the UK for data residency. Outputs are scored objectively using combined CLIP and blinded human review against an 80% acceptance threshold. The success criteria requires that at least one approach meets the 80% threshold at a viable unit cost (assuming £5 to £10 per month license fee).

The resulting innovation is fast, reliable, reproducible, low cost, child-safe character identity across an open-ended set of personalised stories across varied artwork styles.

**Therapeutic story archetypes (PD-02):**

Tomale already drives generation from versioned templates and enforced output schemas. The R&D extends this into a library of story archetypes organised around the topics fathers find hardest to talk about with their children, chosen for those that, left unaddressed, most impede children's social and emotional development and therefore school readiness. Designed with speech and language therapists for age-appropriateness and the safe handling of sensitive subjects, they give a father a structured, lower-pressure way into difficult conversations. The innovation is turning open story generation into purposeful, topic-targeted scaffolds that remove a key barrier to father engagement and channel it toward children's social and emotional development. We will validate that generated stories hold to the intended archetype, stay age-appropriate, and meet the suitability and safety criteria set and rated by the SLTs.

**Father-coaching co-authoring workflows (PD-03):**

Building on the existing chatbot, the R&D develops workflows that coach the father's interaction in real time, prompting the open questions, expansions and modelling that drive children's language and eliciting the child's talk, within the chosen archetype and behind child-safety guardrails. The innovation is a layer that scaffolds the adult's behaviour rather than only producing a story. Fidelity to the therapeutic technique and safety pass rates will be measured, extending the platform's existing moderation states, with human-in-the-loop parental approval gating any content before it reaches a child.

**Engagement instrumentation layer (PD-04), TRL 7 Operational Software Platform (PD-05):**

Reporting & analytics capturing session frequency, duration, initiation and completion, as well as at home learning engagement metrics. The integrated, pilot-ready build combining the above into a unified, operationally complete mobile or web application.

**Ensuring a valid, deliverable approach:** 

Each component carries a defined baseline and acceptance criteria, so progress is measured rather than asserted. Development is iterative and gated, with fallback to the current pipeline if a component underperforms. The SLTs validate therapeutic fidelity and the independent evaluator validates child outcomes, separating delivery from evaluation. Scientific merit comes from the benchmarked consistency and fidelity results. Commercial merit comes from a working platform and feasibility evidence that de-risk adoption through SLT services and early-years settings. Environmental impact is low, using efficient batched inference and reducing reliance on printed materials.

**What completion achieves:**

A successful pilot demonstrates that a father-targeted, SLT-scaffolded co-creation tool increases father's engagement at home and is associated with measurable gains in children's communication and language and personal, social & emotional development, producing the feasibility evidence required to justify Phase 2 and real-world implementation.

## Q8. State of the art & IP (≤400 words)

**Similar products and differentiation**

Adjacent products exist, but none addresses this challenge. Personalised book apps (Wonderbly, Librio) offer name customisation with no developmental purpose. AI story generators (StorySpark, Bedtimestory.ai) create one-off stories without safeguarding, structure or father focus. Specialist SLT tools (ThinkSmartBox, Echolab) target children with severe needs using specialised devices, not fathers in the home. Evidence-based parent interaction programmes such as Hanen's It Takes Two to Talk use strategies like OWL (observe, wait, listen) to coach parental technique and are proven to work, but they require practitioner-delivered adult-to-adult training and are not codified or reinforced between sessions. Emerging research (ContextQ, Apple 2024) explores contextual questioning for children but remains a research prototype with no father focus or SLT design.

Tomale v2.0 is the first product to embed this coaching into a scalable, father-led, home-based tool.

**Novel concepts and approaches**

The innovation spans four areas. First, a coaching-layer chatbot that scaffolds the father's interaction in real time, prompting the open questions, expansion and modelling that the evidence base shows drive children's language development, but delivering it through AI during every co-authoring session without a practitioner present. This codifies what Hanen and OWL demonstrate works into a systemised, repeatable, scalable format. Second, a library of story archetypes designed with SLTs, organised around topics fathers find hardest to broach and that most impede children's social and emotional development. Third, a character-consistency illustration method using reference-conditioned generation with per-character adapters and latent preservation, addressing a problem current generative models do not solve reliably. Fourth, objective in-app measurement of paternal engagement, replacing self-report.

**IP and freedom to operate**

Tomale.ai Ltd owns its existing platform as Background IP and will own the project's Foreground IP. The new components build on our own platform and commercial AI APIs under standard terms, with no third-party rights blocking commercialisation and a provider-swappable architecture to manage dependency risk. The Authority and Crown receive a royalty-free, non-exclusive licence for their own use; third parties are licensed at fair market price, preserving our route to market.

**Subcontractors and handling IP issues**

Subcontractor agreements will assign or licence Foreground IP to Tomale, with terms compatible with the head contract. Foreground IP will be recorded in the register as created, third-party API terms confirmed before use, and outputs protected by copyright and trade secret, with patentable inventions considered.

## Q9. Project plan & methodology (≤400 words) — milestones SMART, monthly payment schedule


**Management  
  
**

The project runs 12 months (Aug 2026 to Jul 2027), managed with PRINCE2 Agile for stage-gated delivery and a Double Diamond approach for co-design, tracked in Linear and GitHub. A month-1 steering group (SLTs, independent educational advisor, independent evaluator, parent representatives) governs assessment criteria, chatbot workflow and archetype design, safeguarding and data protection. The total budget is £366,460. The Gantt appendix details 12 monthly milestones (Mx) with SMART criteria, associated deliverables (PD-xx), verifiable evidence and payment amounts.

**Resources**

- Kyle Burke (project lead, 1.0 FTE, 240 days) and a backend engineer (AWS Bedrock/SageMaker, 1.0 FTE, 240 days) deliver PD-01 through PD-05.
- NRG (65 consulting days plus 120 clinical hours) leads co-design and pilot delivery.
- Dr Cummins (43 days from M3) provides independent evaluation.
- Mrs. Kelsall (10 days) provides EYFS educational oversight.
- All supported by UK-based cloud infrastructure and participant costs.

**Prototype development and feasibility**

The prototype develops sequentially: PD-01 image pipeline (M1 to M4), PD-02 archetype library (M2 to M5), PD-03 coaching chatbot (M3 to M6), integrated and approval-gated as PD-05 (M5 to M7), then tested with 30 families in a 4-month supervised home pilot (M8 to M11).

PD-01 is validated by combined CLIP and blinded human review against an 80% threshold. PD-02 and PD-03 are gated on SLT-approved child-safety criteria. Commercially, the image work targets the unit economics that currently prevent scaling, while UK data residency keeps school, nursery & NHS markets viable.

**Success criteria and evaluation**

- SC1: At least one image approach meets the 80% threshold at viable unit cost (evaluated by benchmarking report, M3).
- SC2: Integrated prototype passes SLT safety & fidelity gate (evaluated by NRG sign-off, M7).
- SC3: 30 pairs recruited, baselined and retained through 4-month pilot (evaluated by consent records and retention data, M8 to M11).
- SC4: Measurable paternal engagement uplift (evaluated independently by Dr Cummins using PD-04 analytics, M12).
- SC5: Improvement in C&L and PSED outcomes (evaluated by Dr Cummins with educational oversight from Mrs. Kelsall, M12).

**Risks**

- Technical: image quality or safety failure, mitigated by dual-approach benchmark, objective gate, human-in-the-loop approval and fallback to current pipeline.
- Commercial: unit economics and adoption, mitigated by cost-comparison.
- Environmental: compute footprint, mitigated by scale-to-zero infrastructure.
- Operational: solo-founder dependency, mitigated by dedicated backend engineer.
- Recruitment: mitigated by NRG contacts, realistic cohort size and at-home usage.
- Ethics: independent review submitted M1 with no NHS or university dependency.
- Cummins: KCL due diligence initiated day 1 with Dr Williams (Southampton) as fallback.

The backend engineer is recruited at £85,000, a fair market rate for a mid-to-senior AWS engineer with Bedrock, SageMaker and SDXL deployment experience. Both roles are project-dedicated and directly deliver PD-01 through PD-05.

Subcontracting (£101,300) covers specialist services unobtainable in-house: NRG provides RCSLT-registered SLTs at standard clinical and consultancy rates for co-design, pilot delivery and outcome documentation. Dr Cummins provides independent evaluation and speech-as-digital-biomarker analysis at KCL academic day rates. Mrs Kelsall provides independent educational advisory input at a rate consistent with specialist EYFS consultancy. No profit is added to any subcontractor line.

Materials (£15,000) cover AWS cloud infrastructure (Bedrock API, SageMaker GPU training, S3) and AI inference costs. UK-region deployment is required for children's data residency.

Overheads and other costs (£44,960) comprise overheads at 10% of labour, an own-calculation rate appropriate for a two-person startup with no premises lease or administrative staff. Other costs include participant incentives and keepsake books for 30 families, ethics review, enhanced DBS checks, professional insurance, co-working workspace at Manchester Science Park, travel and project reporting.

**Value for money.** £366,460 funds three things the taxpayer cannot otherwise easily obtain. A child-safe, UK-sovereign AI illustration pipeline with scalable unit economics. An SLT-designed father-engagement intervention framework ready for NHS, local authority and early-years procurement at fair market price. And rigorous Phase 1 feasibility evidence on engagement uplift and child language outcomes. The CfI contract grants the Crown a royalty-free, UK-wide licence to use the Foreground IP, embedding direct public value. Over 75% of the project constitutes R&D, Tomale's direct spend is 72% of the total, and payments are monthly in arrears against verified milestones.

**Phase 2 indicative cost.** Phase 1 delivers a validated, production-ready technical platform (PD-01 through PD-05), eliminating the need for significant further software development. A Phase 2 multi-site RCT with 200 to 300 father-child pairs is therefore primarily a clinical delivery and evaluation exercise, with the technical deliverables being directly reusable. Indicative Phase 2 cost is £800,000 to £1 million over 18 to 24 months.

## Q12. Commercial potential (≤400 words)

The customer is a father of a child (age 3 to 5) wanting to support his child's language & social-emotional development at home but lacking confidence, technique or time. Current options don't serve him well. Traditional phonics tools feel like homework, generic AI story apps lack developmental purpose, SLT services are inaccessible (Over 65,000 children on NHS waiting lists in late 2024, 46% waiting more than 12 weeks) or expensive (£65 to £120/hour privately).

**Marketable product ad route to market.** The product is a subscription-based co-authoring & coaching app delivered through three channels: B2C subscription, B2B licence to SLT practices, and per-setting licence to nurseries & schools. The B2B SLT route is the priority channel: SLTs work with the target population, recommend usage between sessions & support positive outcomes. NRG provides immediate access via the RCSLT network. The Disabled Children's Partnership estimates unmet speech and language needs cost the UK economy up to £8 billion annually, and modelling indicates every £1 invested in enhanced SLT generates approximately £6.43 in lifetime earnings, underpinning a case for NHS procurement. Longer-term, inclusion in NICE-recommended SLT pathways and Integrated Care System commissioning frameworks would enable further adoption funded by existing budgets.

**Timescales and delivery plan.** Phase 1 evidence (PD-06) arrives July 2027. A Phase 2 proposal could be submitted in Q3 2027 targeting Q1 2028 start. In Q4 2027 Tomale launches a B2C version with the new coaching features, securing anchor clients via NRG's network. Unit economics validated in WP1 enable sustainable scaling. The target subscription price of £5 to £10 per month positions Tomale as a costs-effective booster to private SLT sessions.

**Competitive advantage.** The coaching layer (PD-03) is the primary differentiator: AI scaffolds the father's interaction technique in real time, with no equivalent competition. Combined with SLT-designed archetypes (PD-02) and character-consistent illustration (PD-01), this creates multi-layer IP that applies to Tomale's wider product range and establishes a unique, defensible position in AI-enabled children's storytelling software.

**Existing relationships and international markets.** Tomale has an existing platform at TRL 7 with registered users. NRG provides an active SLT delivery & referral network. Two primary schools & three nurseries in the North West have confirmed interest. International expansion targets English-language markets & the international schools sector. The global EdTech language learning market is valued at $11.7bn (2024), forecasted $124.7bn by 2034, with English the largest segment at 22.6%.
